title: Testing hypotheses via orthogonalization
summary: Classical hypothesis testing frameworks break down in contemporary settings in which null hypotheses are increasingly abstract, the same data are used to both generate and test hypotheses, and minimal assumptions about the underlying data are made. In this work, we propose a new framework for conducting valid hypothesis tests in broad contexts. We propose to add and subtract external noise generated from a symmetric shift-family to our data, $X$, to partition it into two pieces, $X^{(1)}$ and $X^{(2)}$.
